verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI documents deferred tools that can require user approval before running. Its coding agent also offers workspace-rooted file access and an allowlisted shell, which together give per-tool permission gating and scope restriction. Nothing documents sandboxed or isolated execution: workspace rooting and allowlisting restrict scope but are not process or container isolation, and 'executed externally' is not described as a sandbox. Missing for 10: documented sandboxed execution environment, fine-grained per-tool permission policy configuration beyond approval gating, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can restrict what an agent may do with fine-grained tool permissions and sandboxed execution

citations.quote: Pydantic AI provides the concept of deferred tools, which come in two flavors documented below: tools that require approval, tools that are executed externally
it may need to be approved by the user first
